description: Charlie Brouwer is a Virginia artist known for his sculptures, installations, and mixed media drawings. He previously taught at Radford University from 1987 - 2008 before transitioning to a full-time artist, exhibiting over 300 times in his career. This collection highlights select drawings and models from various exhibits that are currently housed at his studio in Floyd, Virginia. His studio website can be visited at https://www.charliebrouwer.com/.

description: This collection contains an interactive tour of the coronal section of an adult wild-type mouse brain, showing Nhlh2 mRNA and Snhg14 long non-coding RNA colocalization in different regions of the brain. description: Located to the South of Ypres in Flanders, Hill 80 was a part of the fighting between the Allied and Central Powers throughout WWI. These objects help archaeologists find out who was fighting, and when, with astonishing accuracy. As you begin to move through this space, note that the artifacts in this exhibit are primarily grouped by their date of use and find location around Hill 80. Each section highlights the variety of nationalities represented by the objects found around this site indicates that fighting took place here continuously between 1914 and 1918.
items.title: Hill 80

description: The Rick Boucher Papers, 1968-2017 (bulk 1975-2011), document his career in the Virginia State Senate, 1975-1982, and in the United States Congress as the Representative of Virginia's 9th District, 1983-2011. The collection consists of press releases, Boucher's writings, mailers he distributed, information about his campaigns and elections, scripts of speeches he gave, news clippings about him and issues he worked on, correspondence, information about grants that he worked on, and audiovisual materials including photographs, VHS tapes, video reels, audio cassettes, DVDs, awards, and digital files. Materials primarily span from the beginning of his political career in 1975 to his retirement from Congress in 2011.

Photographs depict 4-H activities, home demonstration work, food, breeding, field stations, gardening, poultry, dairy, and other subjects. The Extension Division, which was established in 1966, became the Virginia Cooperative Extension and Agricultural Experiment Station Division in 1995, often shortened to the Virginia Cooperative Extension (VCE).

description: The Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University Insect Collection is the oldest and largest entomological collection in Virginia. Founded in 1888 by W.B. Alwood at the university's first experimental station with just a few insects collected from his apple orchards, the collection now composes more than 500,000 specimens. The collection contains many entomological treasures like American Burying Beetles collected from Blacksburg in 1889 (now extinct from the state), colorful Malaysian butterflies, a herbarium of plant pests, and an extensive slide collection of 50,000 soil mites. In addition to pinned dried specimens, the VTEC holds an alcohol collection of aquatic insects and Appalachian millipedes.
items.title: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University Insect Collection
